title: HDD.DRV's kernel-facing half beyond the entry: hddabi, hdcom, mount, hdsvc, hdxms
summary: The kernel-facing contract holds up, and it is better defended than it first appears. Every partition BPB goes through the kernel's rules 3-16. hd_blk's 32-bit HDV_LEN fence is the one bound that knows where a partition ends. Base plus offset cannot wrap. The DRVV_READY system-volume bank is closed by drv_nostamp. The gaps are at the trust edges and in transport retries. First, HDV_ARM takes the caller's segment unchecked. Nothing disarms an arm whose owner died, so a later rung-1 read into a reused claim goes to XMS. Second, rung 0 fails an ECC-corrected read (int 13h status 11h). Third, rung 1 never retries. Fourth, the partition table is trusted on type and length alone, and hd_chs bounds at cylinder 1,024 rather than at the drive's own count. Fifth, HSV_MOUNT skips hd_mount's duplicate guard. On size, about 386 resident bytes serve only the tool. There are three free savings: -11, -4 and -2. The image is 4,096 bytes with 2 spare. Verification refuted none of the 14 findings. It corrected two. hdk-1's proposed DX>=ES fence is unsound, because the Video Player arms a separate heap claim. hdk-2's door widening is SPEC 117.4's deliberate design, so only the stale verb counts remain. Of the 26 doc mismatches, 24 are carried with corrected text. A 25th fix is added: mount.inc's hd_vol_of citation, which the reviewer noted but did not carry. Two are dropped. SPEC 52.11.1's 'twelve verbs' is accurate for shipped builds. os88api.inc:3490 sits inside OSAPI_DRV_CALL's fingerprinted contract and needs an abilock --update.

strengths.title: hd_blk's HDV_LEN fence is the one bound that knows where a partition ends
strengths.why: The kernel is told 'unknown' past 32MB, so its rule 13 checks nothing there. Below 32MB rule 13 trusts DV_SECS, which is the table entry. The driver compares the transfer's 32-bit end against the partition's whole length before it adds the base, so an overstated BPB can never reach the next partition.

strengths.title: HMB_BAD and HMB_NONE are different answers
strengths.why: A failed LBA 0 read and a missing signature both leave a blank buffer, but only the second permits a commit. That prevents a marginal LBA 0 from formatting through live partitions.

strengths.title: The twin take is proved, not assumed, and an ambiguous match pairs with nothing
strengths.why: Pairing is keyed on geometry. The proof is LBA 0 read through both rungs plus a 55AA check, and more than one candidate cancels the pairing. This is Windows 3.1 WDCTRL's take-from-the-BIOS idea, with a stronger proof.
strengths.evidence: drivers/hdd/hdd.asm:906-994 (hd_at_dup), 1056-1114 (hd_twins); kernel/disk.inc:3737-3780 (the take is one word store)

strengths.title: The run-once code is the partition buffer
strengths.why: 508 bytes of attach and ready code live in hd_mbr's 512-byte window, and assembly asserts keep hd_cfgbuf clear of hd_ready. That puts the 4KB claim where it is.

strengths.title: Everything that crosses the seam is treated as hostile
strengths.why: Every device index the tool passes is checked by hd_dev_row_ck. HSV_MSG range-checks its code. The tool image is validated as it arrived: magic, format, link base, dispatcher bytes and HD_ABI_VER.

strengths.title: IDE waits are bounded in seconds and a floating bus is answered at once
strengths.why: This avoids Linux's pre-5.11 hang and also survives a drive spinning up from standby.

strengths.title: A saved geometry does not travel between machines; a mount preference does
strengths.why: The probe's answer wins unless the record says the user typed the geometry, which closes FIELD-NOTES 33.

strengths.title: The XMS read's map is exact
strengths.why: A sector that reached the buffer by any other road leaves its bit clear. The range test is a signed segment difference plus a whole-sector check, so a sector below the armed buffer is refused.

findings.title: HDV_ARM redirects any rung-1 read into the armed segment, including the kernel's own metadata reads
findings.detail: hd_xa_arm validates the CPU, CX and A20 but never checks DX, the segment, against the caller. hd_xfer_ide asks hd_xa_read about every rung-1 read, which includes the FAT window, directory sectors, dsk_secbuf and the cache. With a wrong DX, a FAT-window load lands in XMS while dsk_fatw0 names the new range, and the next dskw_flush writes the stale window back as that range's FAT. The door's stated safety, 'writes are never redirected', misses that a redirected metadata read becomes a wrong write. Separately, an arm outlives its owner: nothing disarms on instance teardown, and a fault between ARM and DISARM leaves a freed segment armed. The one in-tree caller (vp_harm) passes the right DX.
findings.recommendation: Do NOT fence DX against ES. The buffer is a separate heap claim and may sit below the package. For the wrong-DX half, the kernel should tag its user-data DSV_BLK reads with a spare AL bit and the driver should redirect only those (a DSV_BLK contract change, recorded for the flag day). For the stale arm, the kernel's instance teardown should send the driver a disarm, or an arm should expire when the READ_SEQ that it brackets returns.
findings.bytes_est: record: a DSV_BLK contract change; a teardown disarm is a few bytes of kernel plus a DSV verb
findings.prior_art: OS/2 1.x DevHlp Lock/VirtToPhys: the kernel, not the client, establishes that a buffer is the requester's
findings.verify_note: Confirmed in code: hd_xa_arm (hdxms.inc:72-106) validates the CPU, CX and A20, never DX. hd_xa_on is cleared only by ARM and DISARM, with no teardown path, and hd_xfer_ide consults it on every rung-1 read (hdd.asm:482). The proposed `cmp dx, es` fence is UNSOUND. The Video Player's buffer is a separate heap claim, not its own segment: video.asm:6501 says 'DX:BX = the claim', and :7344 says vp_ring is 'placed at THE GAP from the bank'. A heap claim may lie below the package's segment, so the fence would refuse legitimate arms. The record form, where the kernel vouches for the buffer, still stands for the wrong-DX half. Neither form closes the stale arm left by a dead owner. That needs a kernel-side disarm at instance teardown, or an arm that expires. Not in either queue.

findings.title: The package door now reaches a partition erase, and five places still say it reaches no sector
findings.detail: HDV_TOOL forwards to HDT_PKG. Its HDI_GO with CH bit 0 erases and reformats a partition (MBR, FATs, VBR) through hd_raw, and any .O88 can call it. The real fence is the engine's hd_iact_ok together with the wizard's own confirm, not the verb list. hdxms.inc:34-36, hdd.asm:1569-1572, os88api.inc:3490-3493 and 3550, and SPEC 52.1.4 (103347) all still argue 'two verbs, no sector'.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the five passages (mismatches 14-18). Decide explicitly whether a package may erase without a confirm owned by the tool. The cheap strengthening is in HDDTOOL rather than the resident: HDI_GO with erase requires a token returned by HDI_SLOTS.
findings.bytes_est: 0 resident; ~+10 tool for a confirm token
findings.verify_note: The door does reach HDI_GO's erase (hdxms.inc:58-61; os88api.inc HDV_TOOL/HDI_GO). But this is SPEC 117.4's DELIBERATE design: 'It reaches a third now, and still no sector', and 'refuses with HDG_FAIL whatever hd_iact_ok refuses ... the confirm is the wizard's Confirm page'. So the finding is a stale-count consistency issue, severity low rather than medium. The places that still say two verbs are hdxms.inc:34-36, hdd.asm:1569-1572, os88api.inc:3490 and 3550, and SPEC 52.1.4. All but os88api.inc:3490 are fixed below. That line sits inside OSAPI_DRV_CALL's indented contract, so tools/abilock.py fingerprints it, and a fix needs `abilock.py --update` (no bump). It is dropped from the auto-applied set for that reason. Whether a package may erase without a tool-owned confirm remains a policy question.

findings.title: Rung 0 fails a read the controller ECC-corrected (int 13h status 11h)
findings.detail: hd_xfer's rung 0 retries any CF=1 three times with an AH=00h reset between attempts, then fails. Status 11h means the buffer holds corrected data, and DOS-era fixed-disk code accepts it. On an MFM drive behind an ST-11M or WD1002, which is the owner's 5150 class, a weak sector that is corrected every time is unreadable through HDD.DRV. The kernel's BIOS path for an un-taken boot partition has no 11h handling either. Marked PLAUSIBLE: the exact XT-controller behaviour on a multi-sector command needs the field machine.
findings.recommendation: On AH=11h, accept a one-sector run as done. For a longer run, re-issue one sector at a time so the corrected sector is accepted on its own. Raise the same rule for the kernel's BIOS loop with diskread.
findings.prior_art: MS-DOS IBMBIO fixed-disk path treats ECC-corrected as success; RBIL int 13h status 11h
findings.verify_note: Rung 0's .attempt loop retries every CF=1 three times with an AH=00h reset and then fails (hdd.asm:336-364). AH=11h is never examined. kernel/disk.inc has no 11h handling either: grep finds only int 11h equipment-word hits. Whether an XT controller stops at the corrected sector on a multi-sector command is still a field-machine question, as the report says.

findings.title: Rung 1 has no retry and no reset
findings.detail: A select timeout, a DRQ wait that saw ERR or timed out, or an end-of-command ERR/DWF all fail the transfer on the first attempt. Rung 0 gets three attempts and the floppy ladder gets more. hd_buf_step has already left hd_lba and hd_bofs on the failing sector, so a retry is just a re-entry at .run.
findings.recommendation: Add one re-issue from the failing sector, with a counter. Optionally add SRST through base+206h plus a re-issue of hd_ide_setparams between attempts.
findings.prior_art: Linux libata EH (reset, retry); DOS Abort/Retry/Ignore
findings.verify_note: Every failure in hd_xfer_ide goes to hd_xfer_fail4, or to the 0Ah exit after the end-of-command check (hdd.asm:449-527), with no counter and no re-issue. hd_buf_step has advanced hd_lba/hd_bofs only past completed sectors, so re-entering at .run is a valid retry point.

findings.title: The partition table is trusted by type and length alone: no status-byte, duplicate or overlap checks
findings.detail: Two gaps. First, a superfloppy's LBA 0 (FAT at LBA 0) carries 55AA, so it reads as HMB_OK and its boot code becomes four garbage entries. A plausible one can be Deleted or Formatted, which writes a table over a live filesystem. Second, hd_vol_find keys on (device, slot), so two slots with the same base mount twice: two icons and two FAT caches over the same sectors.
findings.recommendation: In hd_part_load (hdcom.inc, so both images), treat any entry whose status byte is not 00h or 80h as HMB_BAD. In hd_mount_one, refuse a base equal to a live row's HDV_BASE on the same device.
findings.verify_note: hd_part_load accepts any LBA 0 carrying 55AA as HMB_OK (hdcom.inc:204-207). hd_part_isfat/hd_part_used check only the type and a non-zero length, never the 1BE+16n status byte. hd_vol_find keys on (HDV_DEV, HDV_PART), so two slots with the same HP_LBA mount twice.

findings.title: hd_chs bounds the cylinder at 1,024, not at the drive's own count, though its contract says 'past the drive'
findings.detail: An LBA between the drive's last cylinder and 1,023 goes to the ROM or the task file as it is. The result depends on the controller: a seek error, an IDNF, or a wrap. A partition entry that overstates its length is therefore refused nowhere until a write near the end fails.
findings.recommendation: Replace cmp ax,1024 with cmp ax,[di+HDD_CYL] (both 3 bytes). Caveat: a rung-1 row taken from the BIOS keeps the BIOS's cylinder count, which may be one short of IDENTIFY's. Either set HDD_CYL from IDENTIFY in hd_twins on success, or accept and document the lost last cylinder.
findings.verify_note: hd_chs is `cmp ax, 1024 / jae .bad` (hdcom.inc:142) and never reads HDD_CYL, while its header says 'past the drive'. The kernel's own BIOS path uses the same 1,024 ceiling (disk.inc dsk_cylmax), so the two agree with each other but not with the drive. The 0-byte swap and its BIOS-cylinder caveat are right. The header text is fixed below.

findings.title: HSV_MOUNT does not refuse a partition that is already mounted
findings.detail: hd_mount guards with hd_vol_find and hd_kvol before calling hd_mount_one. hd_svc_mount calls hd_mount_one directly, and hd_mount_one repeats neither guard. Both installer call sites unmount first, so nothing misbehaves today. But the resident owns the volume table, and its rule depends on the tool's call order.
findings.recommendation: Move the guard into hd_mount_one; hdk-5's base check subsumes it. Then delete hd_mount's own hd_vol_find test.
findings.verify_note: hd_svc_mount (hdtool.inc:597-624) calls hd_part_load, hd_part_ent and then hd_mount_one directly. hd_mount_one (mount.inc:124-188) repeats neither hd_vol_find nor the HDK_IDE gate that hd_mount applies before a kernel-volume take. So HSV_MOUNT on a rung-0 partition the kernel already adopted would also TAKE it, which hd_mount refuses. Harmless today, because the installer unmounts first.

findings.title: hd_mount_one's CF is read as a verdict but is undocumented and partly accidental; the read is redundant
findings.detail: The header says 'clobbers: flags'. hd_svc_mount nevertheless branches on CF. On the .badvol path that CF is OSAPI_VOL_DEL's. The answer is right only because hd_vol_of runs next and supplies both the index and CF.
findings.recommendation: Delete jc hd_svc_out at hdtool.inc:620 so that hd_vol_of is the whole answer, and correct the header.
findings.verify_note: Spot-check. hd_mount_one's .badvol exit leaves hd_unmount_row's OSAPI_VOL_DEL CF and sets no hd_msgc, and hd_svc_mount branches on it (hdtool.inc:619-620). hd_vol_of answers 0FFh/CF itself, so the jc is redundant. It is a 2-byte short jcc. The header is fixed below.

findings.title: DSV_CPNAME publishes a copy of the name the header already holds at +16
findings.detail: hd_s_page 'Hard Drive',0 (11 bytes) duplicates OS88_DRIVER's NUL-padded name field in the same segment. RAM DISK's rd_name (9 bytes) and NET's net_cpname (8 bytes) are the same pattern.
findings.recommendation: Publish dw DRV_ORG+16 (correct in the HMA copy too) and delete the string. Add a note in os88drv.inc that the header's name is a NUL string to publish rather than copy.
findings.verify_note: Spot-check. hd_s_page 'Hard Drive',0 (11 bytes, hdd.asm:838) is referenced only by DSV_CPNAME (hdd.asm:1555). OS88_DRIVER emits the same name NUL-padded at +16. Byte 31 is DRV_H_BSSP, but the 10-character name's NUL at +26 terminates it first, so `dw DRV_ORG+16` works in both images.

findings.title: Ask OSAPI_VOL_SYS for the system volume instead of banking one at DRVV_READY
findings.detail: hd_ready banks OSAPI_FILE_HERE into hd_tvol/hd_tcwd. That depends on the drv_nostamp kernel fix and on DRVV_READY being sent inside drv_load's bracket. OSAPI_VOL_SYS answers the question directly, the banked directory is always the root, and the tool's own page already uses the cell.
findings.recommendation: Replace the two loads with xor dx,dx / call OSAPI_VOL_SYS and delete hd_tvol/hd_tcwd.
findings.verify_note: drv_mounted stands at [dsk_bootvol]'s ROOT, cluster 0 (drvvol.inc:46-56), so the banked hd_tcwd is always 0. OSAPI_VOL_SYS answers BL = the boot volume with no I/O. The resident saving is the 8 bytes of loads at hdtool.inc:128-129 plus 3 of data, less the 7 for `xor dx,dx`/call: -4. The 13 bytes saved in hd_ready are in the run-once hd_mbr window, not resident.

findings.title: The seam copies resident state through six verbs; publish pointers to it at HDT_INIT instead
findings.detail: HSV_SYNC, STATE, SEL, MSG and VOLOF, plus hd_vol_of, exist only to copy bytes the resident owns. HSV_PAGE and HSV_CTRS are table entries pointing at hd_svc_unk. About 386 resident bytes in all serve only the tool. The row layouts are already a written ABI (hddabi.inc), and HD_ABI_VER refuses a mismatched pair. Handing over five separate far pointers keeps declaration order meaningless and ends the sync-before-act discipline.
findings.recommendation: HDT_INIT returns far pointers to hd_devs, hd_vols, hd_ndev, hd_sel and hd_msgc. The tool reads them directly and writes SEL and MSG directly. Only the verbs with side effects keep handlers: RAW, MOUNT/UNMOUNT(+DEV), GEOM and CFGMARK. Bump HD_ABI_VER to 8.
findings.listed_as: ABI-BREAK-LIST P2 (HD_ABI_VER private, moves freely); touches L3 (mega_gpfix serves HDD<->HDDTOOL)
findings.verify_note: Spot-check. The map's seam span C476-C5E4 is 366 bytes, and hd_vol_of is C768-C77C (20). The copy-only handlers (sync, state, volof, msg, sel and their table slots) are roughly 100 of that, so ~-100 is a fair ESTIMATE. HD_ABI_VER is private (ABI-BREAK-LIST P2), and the kern_mega far-call fixup L3 applies as noted.

findings.title: Rung 1 writes one word at a time where it reads with rep insw
findings.detail: The write loop is mov ax,[es:di] / out dx,ax / inc / inc / loop: 8 bytes and about 20 clocks a word on a 286. Banking DS and SI around rep outsw takes 10 bytes and about 5 clocks a word. Writes are multi-sector (data runs and FAT ranges), and an install writes megabytes.
findings.recommendation: Use push ds / push si / mov si,di / push es / pop ds / rep outsw / pop si / pop ds. The +2 bytes fit the 2-byte pad before align 512. Measure it on 86Box mr286 in the final pass.
findings.verify_note: Spot-check. The write loop is 8 bytes (mov ax,[es:di] 3, out 1, inc 1, inc 1, loop 2). The rep outsw form is 10. Nothing after .write reads DI (hd_buf_step uses hd_bofs). The 2 spare bytes are CDFE-CDFF, between hd_mbrok (CDFD) and hd_mbr (CE00).

findings.title: hd_raw's bounce copies CL x 256 words, silently dropping a count's high byte
findings.detail: mov ch,cl / mov cl,al builds the copy count modulo 256 sectors. HSV_RAW passes HRQ_CNT from the tool unchecked, so a run of 256 sectors or more into an HMA or selector buffer moves every sector and copies fewer back. Today's callers use 1-3 sectors.
findings.recommendation: Refuse CX > 127 in the bounce path (cmp cx,127 / ja with CF set), or state the bound in HSV_RAW's ABI line.
findings.verify_note: Spot-check. `mov ch, cl / mov cl, al` (mount.inc:525-526) builds sectors x 256 words modulo 256 sectors. The claim size, (CX+1)/2 KB, is computed from the full CX, so a long run copies short without any refusal. Only HMA or selector buffers take the bounce.

findings.title: hd_buf_step walks DX on an offset wrap, while BLKCAP_SEL promises it walks only BX
findings.detail: hd_buf_step does add [hd_bseg],0x1000 when the offset wraps, which is meaningless on a selector. It is unreachable: a selector's run cannot cross its own 64KB limit, and a run ending exactly at 0x10000 wraps only after its last sector.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line note on hd_buf_step and in 51.8.1 saying why the carry is dead under a selector.
findings.verify_note: Spot-check. hd_buf_step adds 1000h to [hd_bseg] on an offset carry (hdd.asm:659-666). Under a selector, the run cannot wrap before its last sector, so the carry is dead there. A record note is the right size of fix.

doc_fixes.old_text:
; controller card's own ROM, and CHS-only IDE. Everything the user can see is
; here - the Control Panel's Hard Drive page, the disk tool that partitions
; and formats, and the Mount button - because the kernel's half of this is four
; API slots and a volume table, and nothing above them belongs in a kernel
; that boots machines with no hard disk at all.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; controller card's own ROM, and CHS-only IDE: the transport, the volume
; table and mounting, because the kernel's half of this is four API slots and
; a volume table, and nothing above them belongs in a kernel that boots
; machines with no hard disk at all. Everything the user can see - the Control
; Panel's Hard Drive page with its Mount button, the disk tool that partitions
; and formats, the installer - is HDDTOOL.DRV's, read off the system volume on
; demand (SPEC.md 52.11, 52.13).
doc_fixes.why: The page, disk tool, formatter and installer are assembled into HDDTOOL.DRV (hddtool.asm includes cppage/partw/fmt/tool/inst); the resident keeps the probe, both rungs, the volume table and mounting (SPEC.md 52.13).

doc_fixes.old_text:
; WHAT THE KERNEL KEEPS AND WHY. A volume is a small index with 16-bit
; VOLUME-RELATIVE LBAs (SPEC.md 18.7), so the FAT layer, the directory
; walker and the write path are the floppy's, unchanged, and a partition is
; capped at 65,535 sectors - 31.99MB, which is exactly the DOS 3.3 limit
; these machines ran.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; WHAT THE KERNEL KEEPS AND WHY. A volume is a small index with
; VOLUME-RELATIVE LBAs (SPEC.md 18.7), so the FAT layer, the directory
; walker and the write path are the floppy's, unchanged. They were 16 bits,
; which capped a partition at 31.99MB; since SPEC.md 18.7.5 DSV_BLK takes a
; 32-bit one in DI:SI and the cap is FAT16's own (HP_MAXHI:HP_MAXLO,
; 2,047.9MB).
doc_fixes.why: hd_blk takes the LBA's high word in DI (banked in BP) on every kernel that ships HDD.DRV (OS88_BIGVOL; kern_small ships none), and hd_part_big bounds a partition at HP_MAXHI:HP_MAXLO = 3FFED0h sectors, not 65,535.

                                ; in this driver is one sector, so without this

doc_fixes.new_text:

doc_fixes.why: hd_pkg, a few lines below, dispatches a third verb, HDV_TOOL, to HDT_PKG, whose HDI_GO (CH bit 0) erases and reformats; SPEC.md 117.4 says the refusal is hd_iact_ok's and the confirm the wizard's.

doc_fixes.new_text:
direction, so the resident→tool vocabulary was **four verbs** (`HDT_INIT`,
`HDT_FORMAT`, `HDT_INSTALL`, `HDT_SHUT`); `HDT_BUSY`, the five page verbs
(§52.13) and `HDT_PKG` (§117.4) make it eleven. The verb rides `AL`; `BP` is
the tool's entry offset, read out of its own header at +6, because the
dispatcher is `call bp` and `BP` is therefore an address.
doc_fixes.why: hd_tool_call loads BP = [hd_tent] (the image's word at +6) and the verb in AL (hdtool.inc:262-277); hddabi.inc defines HDT_* 0..10.
